requirements_summary:
Workload: chat + RAG (internal), plus summarization (agent assist).

Performance targets (pilot): p95 TTFT <= 350ms (streaming), p95 end-to-end <= 2.5s for ~400-800 output tokens; steady-state 30-60 concurrent users initially, scaling to 300+.

Reliability: needs explicit fallback behavior (model variant/region) disabled by default in regulated mode; change control + rollout policy required.

Security/Compliance: SOC2 report under NDA; encryption in transit + at rest; customer-managed KMS keys; detailed audit logs (who/what/when), export to Splunk; SSO via SAML; configurable retention / log retention guidance; US-only data residency; no training on customer data.

Deployment: Private (VPC) with tight network boundaries; security team requests architecture diagram and ports/egress documentation for approval packet.
notes:
Account context (Northbridge Banking):
- Champion: Director, GenAI Platform (eng) + Security Architect (IAM).
- Buyer signals: security-first, but platform team cares a lot about predictable latency + cost per 1k tokens. They are currently benchmarking multiple vendors and an internal vLLM path.

Discovery highlights:
- They’re building a shared internal "GenAI gateway" for multiple app teams.
- Primary driver is compliance + controllability (auditability, residency, retention), not access to proprietary models.
- They asked early about: SAML/SCIM, audit log contents, retention defaults, and whether any data leaves the VPC.

Pilot outcomes (as captured in closeout):
- Latency/throughput: met pilot SLOs for initial load; some spikes tied to bursty traffic patterns (SE recommended batching/rate shaping).
- Ops/observability: Console dashboards were positively received; they want SIEM-friendly audit export + a clear schema.
- Decision direction: Private deployment is the target; Dedicated discussed only as interim if procurement/implementation timing forces a staged rollout.

Open items:
- Provide: written audit log field list + example payload + export options; retention defaults (what Redwood retains by default vs configurable).
- Confirm: SAML metadata validation fix/workaround documentation (SUP-51214).
- Commercial: procurement kickoff once security signs off; bank likely prefers AWS Marketplace private offer if feasible.
